extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate counsel, accountants, and other preparers of SEC registration statements and periodic reports
extracted.subtask_description: Disclosure requirements and content guidance for Regulation S-K Items 101–105 (Description of Business, Description of Property, Legal Proceedings, Mine Safety, and Risk Factors), including rules for smaller reporting companies and non-GAAP measures, applicable to SEC registration statements and periodic reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP financial measures restrictions (paragraph (e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements governing presentation of non-GAAP financial measures: non-GAAP measures are generally excluded where GAAP, Commission rules, or government/self-regulatory standards require disclosure; non-GAAP measures should be presented outside the financial statements unless required or expressly permitted by the GAAP standard-setter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (e) requirements do not apply to non‑GAAP measures included in communications subject to certain proxy/tender/merger rules (§230.425, §240.14a-12, §240.14d-2(b)(2), §229.1015) or to registered investment companies under the Investment Company Act. For foreign private issuers a non‑GAAP measure otherwise prohibited is permitted if: (1) it relates to the GAAP used in the registrant's primary financial statements; (2) it is required or expressly permitted by that GAAP's standard-setter; and (3) it is included in the registrant's annual report prepared for its home jurisdiction or for distribution to its security holders. Also: non-GAAP measures exclude measures required to be disclosed by GAAP/Commission/governmental rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of smaller reporting company
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and thresholds for 'smaller reporting company': an issuer (not an investment company, asset-backed issuer, or majority-owned subsidiary of a parent that is not a smaller reporting company) that had either (i) public float < $250 million; or (ii) annual revenues < $100 million and either no public float or public float < $700 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is annual. For Exchange Act reporters, public float is measured as of last business day of most recently completed second fiscal quarter and computed by shares held by non-affiliates × last sale (or bid/ask average) in principal market; annual revenues are for most recently completed fiscal year with audited statements. For initial registration statements, public float measured as of a date within 30 days of filing using aggregate worldwide shares held by non‑affiliates plus shares in registration (as applicable) × estimated offering price; revenues as of most recently completed fiscal year with audited statements. An issuer must reflect smaller reporting company status in its Form 10‑Q for the first fiscal quarter of the next year (with option to adopt earlier when newly eligible by public float). Once determined ineligible for exceeding thresholds, issuer remains unqualified unless annual determination finds public float < $200M or both public float and revenues meet charted subsequent-qualification thresholds. Foreign private issuers may not use smaller reporting company requirements unless they use domestic forms and U.S. GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of scaled disclosures available to smaller reporting companies
rubrics_metrics.description: List of Regulation S-K items for which scaled (different/simplified) disclosure is available to smaller reporting companies: Item 101 (Description of business), Item 201, Item 302, Item 305, Item 402, Item 404, Item 407, Item 503, Item 504, Item 601, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A smaller reporting company may comply with either the smaller reporting company requirements or the requirements applicable to other companies for each item, unless the smaller reporting company requirements specifically require compliance with the smaller reporting company rules. The index identifies items with different requirements for smaller reporting companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101 — General development of business
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the general development of the business of the registrant, its subsidiaries, and any predecessor(s); only information material to understanding general development is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure may include, but is not limited to: material changes to previously disclosed business strategy; nature and effects of material bankruptcy/receivership/similar proceedings; material reclassification/merger/consolidation; acquisition or disposition of any material amount of assets other than in ordinary course. For filings other than an initial registration statement, a registrant may forgo a full discussion only if it provides an update disclosing all material developments since the most recent registration/report that included a full discussion and incorporates by reference and includes one active hyperlink to one registration statement or report that includes the full discussion. Special rules apply to registrants that have not received revenue in each of the three prior fiscal years — they must provide plan of operation information depending on filing date relative to second fiscal quarter, including cash runway narrative (and cash budget as supplemental info if used), material R&D, anticipated plant/equipment acquisitions, expected employee changes, and other material areas peculiar to the registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101(c) — Description of business content and segment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the business done and intended to be done, focusing upon the registrant's dominant segment or each reportable segment for which financial information is presented; disclose only information material to understanding the business taken as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure may include: revenue-generating activities, products/services, dependence on key products/customers (including government customers); status of development efforts for new or enhanced products, trends in market demand and competitive conditions; resources material to the business (sources/availability of raw materials; duration/effect of patents/trademarks/licenses); any material portion subject to renegotiation or termination at the government's election; extent of seasonality. If information is material to a particular segment, identify the segment. Also discuss material effects of compliance with government regulations (including environmental) on capital expenditures, earnings, competitive position, including estimated capital expenditures for environmental controls for current fiscal year and any material subsequent period; and describe human capital resources including number employed and any human capital measures/objectives the registrant focuses on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions to Item 101 — Materiality and interperiod comparability for segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on determining what segment information is material and should be disclosed under Item 101(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant should consider both quantitative and qualitative factors such as significance to the registrant (e.g., management's statements about importance), pervasiveness (whether matter affects many items in segment info), and impact (whether it distorts trends). Interperiod comparability may require reporting segment information in current period even if not material by FASB ASC Topic 280 criteria when the segment was significant in the immediately preceding period and expected to be significant in the future. The Commission may permit omission or substitution of comparable information upon written request when consistent with investor protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101(e) — Available information disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether registrant files reports with the SEC and identify those reports; state SEC's internet site address; disclose registrant's internet address, if any; and for certain filers disclose whether annual/quarterly/current reports and amendments are made available free of charge on the registrant's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose: (1) whether you file reports with the SEC and identify them; (2) that the SEC maintains an internet site containing reports and state its address (http://www.sec.gov); (3) your internet address, if any. For accelerated filers or large accelerated filers filing a Form 10-K, disclose whether you make available free of charge on or through your website your Form 10-K, Form 10-Qs, Form 8‑Ks and amendments as soon as reasonably practicable after electronic filing; if you do not, explain why and whether you will provide electronic or paper copies free upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101(f) — Reports to security holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe reports to security holders in any registration statement filed under the Securities Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SEC proxy rules or stock exchange requirements do not require you to send an annual report to security holders or ADR holders, briefly describe nature and frequency of reports you will give to security holders and specify whether reports will contain financial information examined and reported on with an opinion 'by' an independent accountant. For foreign private issuers, if the report will not contain U.S. GAAP financial information, state whether it will include a reconciliation to U.S. GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101(g) — Enforceability of civil liabilities against foreign persons
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign private issuers filing a registration statement under the Securities Act, disclose whether investors can bring actions under U.S. Federal securities laws against the issuer/officers/directors/underwriters/experts who are foreign residents and whether judgments can be enforced when assets are located outside the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must address: (i) ability to effect service of process in the U.S.; (ii) ability to enforce U.S. judgments against foreign persons; (iii) ability to enforce U.S. court judgments in appropriate foreign courts; and (iv) ability to bring an original action in a foreign court to enforce liabilities based on U.S. Federal securities laws. If disclosure is based on counsel opinion, name counsel in prospectus and file a signed consent of counsel to use its name and opinion as an exhibit to the registration statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101(h) — Smaller reporting company business development and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits a smaller reporting company to satisfy Item 101 by describing business development pursuant to paragraph (h), providing information material to understanding general development; if not in business three years, provide same info for predecessors if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business development description should include form and year of organization; any bankruptcy/receivership/similar proceedings; any material reclassification/merger/consolidation or purchase/sale of significant assets not in ordinary course. Business description for smaller reporting company should, to extent material, briefly describe: principal products/services and markets; distribution methods; status of announced new products/services; competitive conditions and competitive position/methods; sources and availability of raw materials and names of principal suppliers; dependence on major customers; patents/trademarks/licenses/franchises/royalty agreements including duration; need for government approval of principal products/services and status if not yet received; effect of existing/probable governmental regulations; costs/effects of compliance with environmental laws; number of total and full-time employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 102 — Description of property
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent material, disclose the location and general character of the registrant's principal physical properties and identify the segment(s) using those properties; if property is not held in fee or is held subject to a material encumbrance, so state and briefly describe how held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction 1: Provide information that reasonably informs investors as to suitability, adequacy, productive capacity, and extent of utilization of principal properties to extent material; comprehensive consideration of materiality is required; descriptions may be collective and detailed physical/legal metes-and-bounds descriptions are not required and shall not be given. Instruction 2: Determine materiality using both quantitative and qualitative factors (see Instruction 1 to Item 101). Instruction 3–7: Registrants in mining operations, oil and gas producing activities and real estate activities must also refer to subparts and guides (§§229.1300–1305, Subpart 1200, Guide 5) and definitions in Regulation S‑X; attention drawn to industry-specific disclosure guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 103 — Legal proceedings disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe briefly any material pending legal proceedings (other than ordinary routine litigation incidental to the business) to which the registrant or any subsidiary is a party or of which their property is the subject, including court/agency, date instituted, principal parties, factual basis alleged, and relief sought. May hyperlink or cross-reference to other legal proceedings disclosure elsewhere in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No disclosure required for routine claims unless they depart from the normal kind of such claims, or for claims where amount involved (exclusive of interest and costs) does not exceed 10% of current assets (unless combined with other similar proceedings). Disclosure must include material bankruptcy/receivership; material proceedings to which directors/officers/affiliates/5% owners or associates are adverse to the registrant or have a material interest adverse to registrant; and administrative/judicial environmental proceedings that are material or exceed thresholds (10% of current assets, or governmental party with potential sanctions exceeding specified thresholds subject to registrant's reasonable belief exceptions). Grouping of similar proceedings and generic description permitted when appropriate. Instruction clarifies thresholds and grouping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 104 — Mine safety disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants that are operators (or have a subsidiary that is an operator) of a coal or other mine must provide specified mine safety information for the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each coal or other mine the registrant or a subsidiary operates, identify the mine and disclose: total number of violations of mandatory health or safety standards under section 104 for which operator received a citation from MSHA; total number of orders under section 104(b); total citations/orders for unwarrantable failure under section 104(d); total number of flagrant violations under section 110(b)(2); total number of imminent danger orders under section 107(a); total dollar value of proposed assessments from MSHA (must provide total proposed assessments regardless of challenge/appeal); total number of mining-related fatalities (report all fatalities unless MSHA determined unrelated to mining). Also list mines that received notice of a pattern of violations or potential pattern under section 104(e), and disclose any pending legal action before the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission, reporting counts and aggregate numbers by specified categories (contests of citations/orders, contests of proposed penalties, compensation complaints, discrimination complaints, temporary relief applications, appeals). Definitions of 'coal or other mine', 'operator', and 'subsidiary' reference statutory/regulatory definitions. Instructions: registrant must provide information as specified by §229.601(b)(95) and include statement that mine safety info required by Section 1503(a) of Dodd‑Frank and this Item is included in exhibit 95; when included in an exhibit to Form 10‑K, provide for registrant's fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 105 — Risk factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a discussion under the caption 'Risk Factors' of the material factors that make an investment in the registrant or offering speculative or risky, organized logically with relevant headings; each risk factor should be set forth under a subcaption that adequately describes the risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of generic risks that could apply to any registrant or offering is discouraged; if included, disclose them at the end of the risk factor section under the caption 'General Risk Factors.' Concisely explain how each risk affects the registrant or the securities being offered. If the discussion is longer than 15 pages, include in the forepart of the prospectus or annual report a series of concise, bulleted or numbered statements no more than two pages summarizing the principal factors that make an investment speculative or risky. If risk factor discussion is included in a registration statement, it must immediately follow the summary section (Item 503) or, if no summary, immediately follow the cover page or pricing information section. The registrant must furnish this information in plain English (see §230.421(d) of Regulation C).
